key_insight: Cold spray can successfully build Fe-6.5 wt.%Si laminates for soft magnetic applications, and annealing improves their magnetic potential by relieving strain and promoting grain growth.
engineering_relevance: This work shows cold spray as a viable additive-manufacturing route for high-Si ferromagnetic laminates, including graded Fe-3.5Si/Fe-6.5Si structures.
method: Cold-spray deposition of Fe-6.5 wt.%Si powder using optimized carrier gas conditions
Microstructural characterization by SEM, EDS, and EBSD
Annealing followed by analysis of a dual-layer gradient Fe-3.5Si/Fe-6.5Si laminate
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful deposition and characterization, with microscopy and EBSD/EDS showing microstructural changes after annealing linked to improved magnetic performance.
watch_item: The results are based on a specific powder system and processing window, so deposition quality and magnetic gains may be sensitive to gas selection, annealing, and layer design.
paper_title: Unraveling the potential of Fe-6.5Si Cold Spray laminates
